items.title: The UK's version of One Nation just got smashed. Could our PM learn from it?
items.description: Britain's unpopular Labour government just scored a thumping by-election victory, but what could look like a blueprint for combating a populist opponent could actually be a warning for Anthony Albanese.

items.title: On health and child care, Labor might have found Pauline Hanson's kryptonite
items.description: Pauline Hanson said thousands of words in her marathon appearance at the National Press Club, but only a few of them will be heard widely.

items.title: Iranian, US negotiators in Switzerland to sort out details to end the war
items.description: US Vice-President JD Vance has landed in Switzerland to meet with Iranian leaders and build on the fragile interim deal to end the war in Iran.

items.title: Colleen Harkin quits Liberal party after praising One Nation
items.description: Liberal Party member and think tank education director Colleen Harkin has quit the party a week after attending a One Nation fundraiser in Melbourne.

items.title: Inside the decades-long hunt for a Long Island serial killer
items.description: Long Island's Ocean Parkway was – for at least one killer – the perfect place to leave a body. With Rex Heuermann behind bars, some questions remain unanswered.

items.title: Scott Miller thinks Australia probably hates him. He's desperate to reverse the damage
items.description: From Olympic silver medallist to convicted drug supplier, Scott Miller opens up on one of the biggest downfalls in the history of Australian sport and the moments that saved his life as he seeks redemption.

items.title: Auction clearance rates fall to lowest level in six years
items.description: Not since the early days of the COVID-19 pandemic have sellers seen such disappointing results at auction, with Cotality predicting "a further loss of momentum" in the housing market.

items.title: Opposition backs Israel's right to military action in Lebanon
items.description: The Shadow Foreign Affairs Minister has defended Israel’s right to continue its military operation in Lebanon, despite an MOU between the US and Iran which commits to an end to the war.

items.title: Why fuel excise cut is being extended by another month but at smaller discount
items.description: The fuel excise cut was due to stop at the end of the month but will continue to a lesser extent until August. Here's why.

items.title: Trump says Reflecting Pool may be drained for repairs after 'vandalism'
items.description: Donald Trump says the newly revamped Reflecting Pool needs "repairs" and that multiple people have been arrested for vandalising the Washington DC water feature.

items.title: Mona unveils $100m underground library packed with rare literary treasures
items.description: From Shakespeare's First Folio to neon-lit shelves to a curvy kids' section, Mona's new library, Phrontisterion, is anything but ordinary.

items.title: Live: Warbrick aerial show gets Storm a win in Munster's milestone match
items.description: Will Warbrick scores three tries in a phenomenal outing to help Melbourne to a 42-20 win over the Raiders in Cameron Munster's 250th NRL match. Follow live.

items.title: Bulldogs get the points at Docklands amid big injury worries for Saints
items.description: The Western Bulldogs get the points at Docklands against St Kilda to finish round 15, as the Saints lose two key players to injury.

items.title: WA football great Cousins taking inspiration from Daniher in MND fight
items.description: WA football great Bryan Cousins is taking inspiration from the late Neale Daniher in his fight with motor neurone disease, as he pays tribute to son Ben for his efforts in combating addiction.

items.title: Bird flu detection 'a distant concern' for Victoria, industry says
items.description: The head of Victoria's peak farming group says the detection of the deadly H5 variant of avian influenza in Western Australia is a "distant concern" for Victorians.

items.title: Love story: Coming out as a throuple
items.description: Everyone is bisexual, polyamorous, and has a crush on me. Or at least, that's my default assumption and the pick-up line that led to my triad with Rhea and Leo.

items.title: How many clothes should you own? The maths behind a sustainable wardrobe
items.description: The environmental impact of a garment often depends on how many times it's worn. In a sense, every additional wear helps "offset" the garment's carbon footprint.

items.title: Is 'baby brain' real? A neuroscientist explains
items.description: The fog new parents feel is real, but it seems to be driven less by motherhood rewiring the brain than by exhaustion, overload and the relentless demands of caring for a tiny human.

items.title: They bought into Australia's tallest tower. Now their deposits are in limbo
items.description: Apartment buyers who were sold on ambitious plans for the tallest building in the country say they're facing up to a decade of uncertainty after the head-turning project faltered.

items.title: Family concerned over disappearance of 47-year-old Victorian man
items.description: The family of Horsham man Neville Nicholson is concerned for his safety and is desperate for his safe return.

items.title: Quick hits: Snakes at Germany's training and a player nicks a ref's watch
items.description: A Curaçao goalkeeper etches out a piece of World Cup history, Germany faces some slippery training pitch invaders and a referee's watch is briefly nicked by a player. Here are today's quick hits.

items.title: Thunderbirds first team through to Super Netball Grand Final
items.description: The Adelaide Thunderbirds are through to their third grand final in four years. Now they wait to see if they will face the Melbourne Vixens or West Coast Fever for a shot at the title.

items.title: Speedway plans spark protest
items.description: Residents of Beachmere in Moreton Bay say a proposed speedway track will “fundamentally change the character" of the small coastal town.

items.title: Student messages mum about 'scary' fight between men on school bus
items.description: Students who witnessed a violent fight between two men on a school bus have been left shaken by the incident.

items.title: Police speech stuns descendants gathered at site of outback mass killing
items.description: Ronnie's great-grandfather collected bones and teeth from an outback creek bed. Now police say they're 'not proud' of what occurred.
